forecast-period.text: A trough of low pressure and cold front about the west, will move over the remainder of South Australia today. Another cold front clips the southeast on Monday, followed by a high pressure system, which will then move across southern parts of the state on Tuesday. A trough of low pressure approaches the western border on Wednesday whilst a cold font moves over waters to the south.
Wind and wave forecasts are averages. Wind gusts can be 40 per cent stronger than the forecast, and stronger still in squalls and thunderstorms. Maximum waves can be twice the forecast height.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones. Marine forecasts are also available on VHF and HF radio. View the radio schedule on www.bom.gov.au/marine
Check the latest Coastal Waters Forecasts for information on wind, wave and weather conditions for neighbouring coastal zones.

forecast-period.warning-summary: Strong Wind Warning for Sunday for South Central Coast
forecast-period.text: West to northwesterly 15 to 20 knots increasing to 20 to 25 knots in the evening. Winds reaching up to 30 knots in the late evening.
Around 1 metre, increasing to 1 to 2 metres by early evening.
Southwesterly 1 to 1.5 metres, decreasing to around 1 metre around midday, then increasing to 1 to 1.5 metres during the afternoon.
Mostly sunny. The chance of a thunderstorm inshore in the late morning and early afternoon.

forecast-period.warning-summary: Strong Wind Warning for Monday for South Central Coast
forecast-period.text: Westerly 20 to 25 knots, reaching up to 30 knots during the morning. Winds turning southwesterly 15 to 20 knots in the late afternoon.
1.5 to 2.5 metres, decreasing to 1 to 1.5 metres by early evening.
Westerly 2 to 3 metres, increasing to 3 to 4 metres by early evening.
Southwesterly 10 to 15 knots becoming variable about 10 knots during the morning then becoming northeast to southeasterly 10 to 15 knots during the afternoon.
Westerly 3 metres, tending southwesterly 2.5 to 3 metres during the morning.
